solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: South American relations found somewhere in the south

parts.note: US, the United States, stands for American
sexual relations, shortened to sex

explanation.surface: A family from South America has settled in a part of southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two abbreviations. SUSSEX is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Sussex is an English county on the south coast, so it is a place in the south of the country.

clue.text: Paddy's conserving time and energy on unknown Mediterranean resort

indicators.note: conserving means keeping inside, so the letter is held within

parts.note: a strop is a paddy, a fit of bad temper
E is the symbol for energy
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: An Irishman saves time and energy on his trip to a mystery Mediterranean resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irishman's name but means a tantrum, a British colloquial word for a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: St Tropez is a glamorous seaside town on the French Riviera, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Roger inside gulps gin, flagrantly having a binge

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the letter goes into the shuffled letters
flagrantly suggests wild, outrageous behaviour, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: Roger is the radio code word for R

explanation.surface: A man named Roger gulps down gin shamelessly on a bender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flagrantly' rearranges GULPSGIN, and R goes inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to indulge extravagantly, so splurging matches being on a spree.

clue.text: Archdeacon supports celeb swiping boundaries for cricket team

indicators.note: in a down answer, the supporting piece sits beneath the other
swiping boundaries means stealing the outer letters, leaving the middle

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A churchman backs a celebrity who hits fours and sixes for a cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a boundary is a shot to the edge of the field, so 'swiping boundaries' sounds like batting; here it strips the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side fields eleven players, so the number serves as a name for the team.

clue.text: Spam Irishman knocked back on boat

parts.note: a junk is a flat-bottomed Chinese sailing boat

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed in the opposite direction, so the name is read from right to left

parts.note: Liam is a typical Irish man's name

explanation.surface: An Irishman is being pushed back aboard a boat, maybe while eating tinned meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spam' looks like the tinned meat but is unwanted email; 'on' just places one piece beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is unsolicited bulk advertising, the electronic equivalent of unwanted circulars through the letterbox.

clue.text: Novel, small gift for president

parts.note: Ulysses is James Joyce's novel
a grant is a gift of money

explanation.surface: Someone gives a book and a little present to the head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S Grant was the Union general who became the 18th President of the United States.

clue.text: Dotty liked to tour yearly, essentially a county in Eire

indicators.note: to tour means to go around, so the shuffled letters surround the middle pair
dotty means crazy, signalling a rearrangement
essentially means at the heart, so only the central letters are used

explanation.surface: An eccentric woman named Dotty liked to visit an Irish county every year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like a name but signals the rearrangement, making KILDE, which 'to tour' wraps round the middle of 'yearly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kildare is a county in the province of Leinster, west of Dublin.

clue.text: Afloat, plan to keep foundations of business somehow

indicators.note: to keep means to hold within, so the picked letters go inside

parts.note: an aim is a plan or intention

indicators.note: in a down answer the foundations are the bottom, so the last letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: A company stays afloat by planning to protect its foundations in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foundations of' picks S and W from the ends of 'business' and 'somehow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswim is a literary adjective meaning floating or swimming in a liquid.

clue.text: Vocal band careless about track name

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the other letters sit inside

parts.note: lax means careless or slack
RY, for railway, is a track

explanation.surface: A sloppy singing group fumbles a song called by name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a music group, but here it is the voice box.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx houses the vocal cords, the bands of tissue in the throat that produce voice.

clue.text: Mark, in language education books, retrospective

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: LIT, short for literature, means books

explanation.surface: A grade given in a review of language textbooks, looking back over the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' turns EDLIT round. 'in language' belongs to the definition: the mark is a written one, as in Spanish, not a grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is the wavy accent sign written over letters in languages such as Spanish and Portuguese.

clue.text: Can fellow reduce the price of spring plant?

parts.note: may and can both express permission
to lower a price is to reduce it

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether a man will knock down the cost of a plant flowering in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb asking a question but supplies a word of permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayflower is a name for several plants that bloom in spring, such as hawthorn and trailing arbutus.

clue.text: Fighter plane's gentlemen maintaining electronic check by hand

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the letter goes within

parts.note: Messrs, plural of Mr, means gentlemen
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in email
CH is the chess abbreviation for check
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Gentlemen give an electronic check to a fighter plane by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The ''s' after 'plane' stands for 'is'; 'by' simply joins CH to MITT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Messerschmitt Bf 109 was a famous German fighter aircraft of the Second World War.

clue.text: Restricted by a particular map, Earl's up the creek without a paddle

indicators.note: restricted by means held within something, so the shuffled letters sit between the two letters for the map

parts.note: OS, Ordnance Survey, is the British national mapping agency, so an OS map is a particular map

indicators.note: up here means stirred out of place, so one letter of the name shifts position

parts.note: the letters of the word, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A nobleman, kept to one map, finds himself in the proverbial creek without a paddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' moves the E of EARLS to the end. OS, Ordnance Survey, makes Britain's official maps. The idiom 'up the creek without a paddle' hides the literal definition at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat lacking oars has no means of being rowed, which is exactly the plight of being without a paddle.

clue.text: Astronaut's injury seen in sick bay

indicators.note: seen in means found inside, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: SAN, short for sanatorium, is a sick bay at a school
harm means injury

explanation.surface: A spaceman's wound is being treated in the medical room.
explanation.walkthrough: Helen Sharman was the first Briton in space, in 1991. The ''s' after Astronaut stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen Sharman flew to the Mir space station in 1991, becoming Britain's first space traveller.

clue.text: Male Norwegian writer I knew somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a Norwegian man who was a writer they knew slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik is a common Scandinavian given name for a man, as borne by many Norwegians.

clue.text: Graduate wrongly dates a piece of furniture

parts.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education graduate

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are set down in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A new graduate gets their dates muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges DATES into STEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedstead is the frame of a bed, an item found in any bedroom.

clue.text: The German and Italian painter one advises about greens?

parts.note: die is a German word for the
Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: A German and an Italian artist, one of whom gives advice on vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' just joins the two pieces. The question mark marks 'greens' as vegetables, a playful example of what such an adviser recommends.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrition expert counsels people on diet, including eating their vegetables.

clue.text: Given a month, European told to publicise Victorian work

parts.note: Jan is short for January

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: to air something is to make it public

explanation.surface: A European is given a month and told to promote a nineteenth-century piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'told' means the word 'air' is heard as EYRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre, Charlotte Brontë's 1847 novel, is a classic of the Victorian era.

clue.text: Good beams of light mature plant in US

parts.note: rays are beams of light
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Fine sunlight helps a plant grow up in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray sage is a shrub of the American West, a sagebrush with greyish leaves.

clue.text: In American university, Queen song tanks

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter goes between the other two

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: A Queen song plays at an American college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the rock band, but only gives Q.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria are glass tanks for keeping fish, the plural of aquarium.

clue.text: It's a performance, making American the ultimate cheese

indicators.note: the ultimate means the last letter, which is swapped for the letter standing for American

parts.note: a fete is a festive show or entertainment

explanation.surface: A show that ends up turning out American, then the best cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making American the ultimate' changes the final E of FETE to A.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined cheese from Greece, made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Throwing game ceases around two in morning

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the picked letter goes inside

parts.note: quits means stops or ceases

indicators.note: two in means the second letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A game of throwing stops at two in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two in morning' looks like a time but picks O, the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoits is a game of tossing rings over a peg, popular at fairs and on ships.

clue.text: Doctor drinks the greatest, most superior cocktail

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
Muhammad Ali called himself the Greatest
U means upper class, the most superior social group

explanation.surface: A doctor drinks the finest, most select cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: Muhammad Ali, the boxer, styled himself 'The Greatest'; U for upper class is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malibu is a cocktail made with coconut-flavoured rum of the same name.

clue.text: Company united in disorderly hunt, using coarse language?

indicators.note: in places one group of letters within the other
disorderly means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for united, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A company joined in a riotous hunt, swearing as they went.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' makes UNTH. The question mark flags that the definition is only an example of the trait.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uncouth is crude and ill-mannered, so foul talk is one way of showing it.

clue.text: Understand cat confused in Switzerland

indicators.note: in means placed within the other letters

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat gets lost and bewildered in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' makes ATC; CH comes from Switzerland's Latin name, Confoederatio Helvetica.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a meaning is to grasp it, as in 'I didn't catch what you said'.

clue.text: Expert holds religious class on Bible about sin

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the other letters sit inside

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: on places one piece after the other
about means turned around, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible
RI is religious instruction, a school lesson

explanation.surface: An expert takes a religious lesson about the Bible's teaching on sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives VA; RI is religious instruction, a British school subject. Avarice is one of the seven deadly sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice, or greed, is one of the seven deadly sins of Christian tradition.

clue.text: Prohibition police backed after Italian club trashed at front

indicators.note: after places the following letters behind the club's name

parts.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club

indicators.note: backed means run backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the detective branch of British police

indicators.note: at front picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Police backed a ban after an Italian football club was trashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at front' sets the T before the police letters, and 'backed' reverses the lot to make DICT.
explanation.definitionFit: An interdict is a formal ban or prohibition, especially an injunction in Scots law or a church censure.

clue.text: Son's removed from European island in a chilling way

indicators.note: removed from means taken out of, so the letter is deleted

parts.note: Sicily is the large Italian island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A boy is chillingly sent away from a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Done coldly or frostily, an adverb meaning with an unfriendly chill.

clue.text: Mike, during school dance, initially lacking sentimentality

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the letter goes inside
initially lacking means losing the first letter

parts.note: the waltz is a ballroom dance
Mike is the radio code word for M

explanation.surface: A boy called Mike at a school dance is shy at first, lacking emotional display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially lacking' leaves ALTZ; 'during' drops M into the middle of the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltz, Yiddish for chicken fat, came to mean excessive, sugary emotion in art or music.

clue.text: One in five children outwardly consume fruit

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five children born together

indicators.note: outwardly takes just the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: One of five siblings eats some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The quince is a hard, aromatic, pear-shaped fruit used for jelly and paste.
